issue.standard_remedy: Map the sub-tier and qualify an alternate
issue.summary: Depends on a single-source sub-tier supplier (North America)

plan.diagnosis: Apollo Chemicals Inc. presents supply chain fragility with a resiliency score of 44 (below acceptable threshold) and reliance on 43 sub-tier suppliers while our organization maintains single-source dependence for USD 1,305,390 in annual spend. Despite zero disruption events in the trailing 12 months, the concentrated sub-tier network in North America creates systemic vulnerability that could cascade to our operations. Root cause is inadequate sub-tier visibility and absence of qualified backup sources for this critical chemical supplier.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct sub-tier mapping exercise with Apollo Chemicals Inc. to identify the critical single-source sub-tier supplier(s) within their 43-supplier network and obtain business continuity plans
Issue RFI to 3-4 alternative chemical suppliers with North America presence to assess technical capability, sub-tier diversity, and resiliency scores above 60
Qualify at least one alternate supplier through technical validation, sample testing, and audit of their sub-tier supply base to ensure dual-source capability
Negotiate contractual sub-tier transparency clause with Apollo Chemicals requiring quarterly disclosure of critical sub-tier dependencies and 60-day advance notice of sub-tier changes
Implement 70/30 split award strategy allocating USD 914,000 to Apollo and USD 391,000 to qualified alternate, with trigger clauses to rebalance if resiliency score falls below 50

plan.expected_impact: Mitigate supply chain risk exposure of USD 1,305,390 by establishing dual-source capability and improving weighted resiliency score to above 55 within 6 months.
kpis: Number of qualified alternate suppliers (target: minimum 1)
Sub-tier visibility coverage (target: 100% of critical sub-tiers mapped)
Supply continuity metric (target: zero disruption events)
Alternate supplier spend allocation (target: 30% or USD 391,607 within 12 months)
risks: Technical qualification of alternates may exceed 90-day timeline if product specifications are highly customized
Apollo Chemicals may resist sub-tier transparency requirements, requiring escalation to executive stakeholder
Dual-sourcing may increase landed cost by 3-8% due to loss of volume leverage on USD 1,305,390 spend
Alternate suppliers may have longer lead times during qualification phase impacting inventory buffers
ERP system complexity across SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, NetSuite and Coupa may delay source list updates and purchase order routing logic
erp_actions: SAP: Create source list (ME01) for affected material codes with Apollo Chemicals (primary, 70% quota) and qualified alternate (secondary, 30% quota); set quota arrangement validity from qualification completion date
SAP: Add vendor sub-range indicator in LFA1 with custom Z-field to flag single-source sub-tier risk and trigger quarterly review workflow
Oracle EBS: Update Approved Supplier List (ASL) to include alternate supplier with 'Preferred' status; configure sourcing rules for automatic PO distribution based on 70/30 allocation
Coupa: Create supplier risk profile for Apollo Chemicals with resiliency score monitoring; set automated alert threshold at score <50 to notify category manager

Dynamics 365/NetSuite: Add alternate supplier to vendor master with payment terms NET45 (vs NET30 for Apollo) to incentivize primary supplier performance; configure purchase order approval workflow to require Category Manager sign-off for chemical purchases exceeding USD 50,000 single PO

All ERPs: Implement vendor performance scorecard integration capturing quarterly sub-tier transparency compliance (25% weighting) and resiliency score (25% weighting) alongside quality and delivery metrics
